question: Can frozen auxiliary good reductions certify Z-linear independence of the two exact rational points in each of the eight final width-eight beam states?
states: all eight states in beam result depth eight, in beam order; no resampling or favorable-state selection
auxiliary_prime_law: all odd primes from 3 through 199 inclusive, ascending, tested for every state
good_reduction: short Weierstrass A,B have denominators coprime to ell and discriminant nonzero modulo ell
point_reduction: for quotient test require both rational point-coordinate denominators coprime to ell and verify reduced points lie on the reduced curve
odd_order_witness: first good-reduction ell with #E(F_ell) odd; then rational E(Q)[2] is trivial by prime-to-ell torsion injection
quotient_witness: first good-reduction ell with both point reductions and P1, P2, P1-P2 outside 2E(F_ell); their images are independent in E(F_ell)/2E(F_ell)
certificate: a state is certified Z-linearly independent only if both witnesses exist; reduction parity plus absence of rational 2-torsion gives infinite descent for every integer relation
recording: retain every prime status, group order and double-image count where computed, point reductions, first witnesses, and uncategorized states; audit independently with Python finite-field arithmetic
claim_boundary: certificate applies to the eight exact rational curves and pairs at fixed 313-adic depth eight; it neither changes the beam selection nor estimates relation yield elsewhere
